subject: International data export and subprocessor lineage

Subject: Initial questions — where is customer data processed and who are subprocessors?

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed to procurement, the security team asked for a short Q&A specific to processing locations and subprocessors. High-level questions below — can you confirm in writing or point us to artifacts?

1) Where does Redwood process our hosted API requests by default (primary region(s))? Do you ever route request tokens or logs outside those regions?
2) Who are the subprocessors that touch request payloads or metadata (e.g., cloud providers, monitoring, logging, telemetry)? Please note any subprocessors with EU presence.
3) Does Redwood perform any cross-border export of raw request data, model keys, or KV cache? If so, under what circumstances?
4) What are the deletion/erasure timelines for customer data (both short-lived caches and persisted logs), and what evidence can you provide that deletion completed?
5) For customers that require EU-only processing, what options do you offer (hosted EU-only, dedicated, private deployment)? Any constraints on functionality?
6) Can you provide SOC2 or equivalent evidence and a current subprocessor inventory?

If you already have a short subprocessor inventory and a residency map, please send them. We need clear statements for our procurement/security review and a list of contractual commitments (DPA/SCCs). Goal is to make a go/no-go decision before Oct 15.

Thanks,
Anna

Hi Anna — Monica on the SE side here. Replying in order with the practical details and attaching what we can. (Attachment: subprocessor_inventory.csv — includes role, region, and data access type.)

1) Default processing regions- Hosted API: requests are routed to the primary region nearest to the calling client by default. For new accounts the regional footprint is typically us-east-1 (primary) with failover to us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for latency optimization.

Note: Routing for our multi-tenant hosted service may cross region boundaries for operational reasons (failover, maintenance). We do not move or replicate customer request payloads outside the primary region for normal processing except for short-lived telemetry used for health/metrics aggregation (see below).

2) Subprocessors (summary)- Primary compute/storage: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west1) for certain model infra- CDN / edge: FastEdge Networks (global) — only metadata and aggregated telemetry- Observability: LogWatch Co. — logs are encrypted in transit and at rest; access limited to on-call ops- Metrics/telemetry pipeline: MetricFlow (US/Europe zones)- Data plane encryption/KMS: AWS KMS / GCP KMS depending on deployment

Full inventory is attached and shows which subprocessors can access PII or request payloads. The CSV also calls out subprocessors with EU-hosted infrastructure.

3) Cross-border exports- For hosted accounts on our standard shared offering, primary inference input/output is processed in the region selected. However:
  - Aggregated telemetry (health/metrics) can be routed to our central observability backends which are primarily US-based for analysis; that telemetry is pseudonymized and limited to request-level metrics (latency, error rates), not full payload content.
  - KV cache used to accelerate response generation is sharded by region; we do not replicate customer KV caches across regions by default. Cache eviction preserves privacy (entries are ephemeral and tied to session keys).

4) Deletion and erasure timelines
  - Short-lived caches (KV cache, ephemeral model context): purged within minutes to hours depending on activity; explicit delete via API or at session end available for Dedicated/Private customers.
  - Request logs (for billing/trace): default retention 90 days; can be shortened via contract for Dedicated or Private deployments.
  - Erasure requests submitted via the console or ticket: for hosted customers we aim to complete the erasure workflow within 30 calendar days; for Dedicated/Private we can agree to shorter SLOs in the DPA.

5) EU-only options
  - Hosted EU-only: we offer an option to restrict processing to EU regions (eu-west-1 / europe-west1) for new accounts. This option limits some multi-region failover behavior and may affect latency for non‑EU users.
  - Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in EU regions with explicit tenancy and contractual controls.
  - Private deployment: VPC or on-prem package — full EU residency and customer-controlled network.

6) Evidence and artifacts- I've attached subprocessor_inventory.csv (columns: vendor, role, regions, access_type, contractual_status) and a residency map image. We will provide SOC2 summary and a formal DPA/SCC addendum.

Notes / caveats:- If you require absolute guarantees that no metadata ever leaves the EU, Private deployment is the recommended path.- For hosted EU-only customers we provide contractual commitments and operational controls, but some aggregated telemetry and platform health data may still flow to Redwood-managed backends for critical operations (pseudonymized).

Happy to hop on a quick 30 minute call to walk the security team through the CSV and map.

Best,

Monica / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attached CSV (we reviewed at a high level). A few follow-ups from our compliance checklist before we advance:

• Can you confirm whether KV cache entries ever get written to persistent blob storage or backups? We need assurance they are never included in backups sent to a different region.
• For the telemetry you described, can you clarify the exact fields included (e.g., do tracing IDs or truncated user identifiers travel off-region)?

• Regarding deletion: we have a hard requirement in our procurement that erasure must be completed within 30 days and that a signed attestation with a deletion report (timestamps + affected data identifiers) be provided. Can Redwood commit to that for hosted accounts or is that only for Dedicated/Private?
• Please send the SOC2 summary and residency map (we need to attach to the security review).

Also provide the contact point for escalation if an export or unplanned cross-border transfer is detected.

Anna

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 15:25:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial questions — where is customer data processed and who are subprocessors?

Hi Anna — Karthik from Privacy & Legal. Thanks for the specific asks; please find the commitments below and attached evidence (SOC2-Summary.pdf, residency-map.png).

1) KV cache persistence- We confirm KV cache entries are in-memory and sharded by region for hosted customers and are not written to durable backups during normal operations. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can configure no-persistence modes and provide architecture notes.

2) Telemetry fields- Aggregated telemetry includes: request latency, HTTP status, model variant, token counts, and anonymized trace identifiers. We do not export raw prompt or response content as telemetry. Trace identifiers are internal IDs and are not mappable to PII without internal lookup controls; access is tightly controlled and logged.

3) Deletion / attestation- Redwood can commit to a 30 calendar day erasure SLO for hosted customers in the DPA for requests submitted via the console or the security ticketing flow. We will provide a deletion attestation that includes timestamps and the types of records removed (e.g., ephemeral cache, request logs). For Dedicated and Private customers we can contract for shorter SLOs and additional audit evidence.

4) Cross-border legal controls- For hosted customers we offer:
  - DPA with EU Data Processing Addendum (includes SCCs)
  - Option to restrict processing to EU regions (hosted EU-only) for new tenants
For customers requiring absolute control (no off-region telemetry), Private deployment is recommended.

5) Escalation contact- Security incidents or suspected exports should be sent to security@redwood.ai and privacy@redwood.ai. For GlobalVitals I will be your designated contract owner and can be reached at karthik.iyer@redwood.ai. We will also open a named support channel in our incident management console if you decide to move forward.

Next steps:
• I have attached SOC2-Summary.pdf and the residency map to this email for your review.
• If this meets your requirements, I will send a DPA (DocuSign) with SCC language and the deletion attestation template.

Regards,
